question.value: Where does [C II] 158 um emission come from (ionized vs neutral gas, via [N II] 205 um), and what are the neutral gas density, FUV field strength and hydrogen mass of z~7 star-forming galaxies from [O I] 145 um?

evidence.quote: Firstly, we examine the fraction of \[C ii\] $158\,{\rm \mu m}$ originating from either ionized gas or neutral gas (both atomic and molecular) using observations of the \[N ii\] $205\,{\rm \mu m}$ emission line.
Secondly, we study the neutral gas properties of star-forming galaxies in the EoR using the \[O i\] $145\,{\rm \mu m}$ observations.
Observations of \[O i\] $145\,{\rm \mu m}$ emission lines of target galaxies were newly performed during ALMA Cycle-9 #2022.1.00446.S (PI: Fudamoto)

referee_caveats_inferred: Only four targets, selected as [C II]-bright, so conclusions are not representative of the general EoR population
R_ion fiducial value 3.6 is the average of a model range 1.5-5.7 and drives the f_PDR limits
A1689-zD1 values are not corrected for lensing in tables while some masses carry a 4.14/mu factor
Gas fraction range differs between the abstract (0.3-0.8) and Section 5.3.2 (0.3-0.9); REBELS-18 abundance differs between text (8.50) and footnote 7 (8.53)
T_ex = 50 K is assumed for all targets, and hydrogen masses rely on ionized-gas JWST abundances applied to neutral gas
REBELS-25 G0 and n_H are adopted by judgement and the Table 4 n_H (~10^6.5) differs from the 10^6 quoted in the Section 5.2.2 text and conclusion
